scope: Synthetic model-only, current identity pack and delegated-work schemas. Not full runtime catalog, STT/TTS, private memory, actual work admission or channel latency.
hypothesis: GPT-6 Luna low may improve short contact latency and quality over GPT-5.6 Luna low on the unchanged provider route.

criteria_before_run.greeting: Warm concise Dutch greeting, no unnecessary tool or claims
criteria_before_run.small_talk_during_work: Answer current small talk, do not answer unfinished research or claim it complete
criteria_before_run.accepted_work: Briefly acknowledge admitted task without claiming completed result
criteria_before_run.selection: Quality must pass all three; prefer lower first-content latency across most cases, with no unsupported availability/latency claim

rows.text: Hallo Jaap, fijn je weer te spreken. Waar kan ik je mee helpen?
Hallo Jaap! Fijn dat je er bent.
Goed, dank je. En met jou?
Goed, dank je. Ik ben er en houd Home Assistant Cloud voor spraak voor je in de gaten.
Ik pak dit op en zet de werking van Home Assistant Cloud voor spraak met bronnen voor je uit.
Ik zoek uit wat Home Assistant Cloud voor spraak biedt en koppel de bronnen erbij terug.

assessment.quality: Both pass the predefined three synthetic response criteria. GPT-6 Luna is warmer/shorter in this sample and answers small talk without drifting to research. Neither executed tools or live work.
assessment.recommendation: Provisional speed candidate only; do not install a config-only switch. Installed Pydantic profile does not recognize GPT-6 Luna native tool search. Correct the bounded compatibility profile before rollout; existing latency comparisons do not establish performance with that correction.
assessment.latency: GPT-6 Luna first content wins greeting and admitted work; loses small talk by 93 ms. Completion wins all three. One sample per case, not a statistical benchmark; full runtime catalog and speech unmeasured.

compatibility_review.method: Inspected installed profiles and captured serialized request bodies with transport replaced by immediate exception before any network operation. Only synthetic probe input used.
compatibility_review.current_profile: gpt-5.6-luna has native tool_search; gpt-6-luna falls back to generic profile without native tool_search or phase support.
compatibility_review.reasoning_effort: Both serialized requests explicitly include reasoning.effort=low and summary=auto; generic profile did not omit the configured effort.
compatibility_review.token_difference: Identical instructions, different wire tool catalogs: baseline sends native tool_search and deferred search_personal_memory; candidate sends only local search_tools function. This explains the structural source of 317-token difference. No tokenizer-level reproduction attempted.
compatibility_review.request_limit_conflict: The local search_tools fallback needs a follow-up request to use discovered actions. Eva phase sets UsageLimits(request_limit=1) and provider attestation requires exactly one request. Thus candidate conversation-only success does not establish functional tool use.
compatibility_review.tool_free_case: Accepted-work case sends no tools with identical instructions; input tokens equal1373; candidate first content800ms versus1290ms. It does not test actual action selection/admission.
compatibility_review.official_support: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna documents reasoning.low and native tool_search support. Existing Astra compatibility override provides a precedent; no shared files modified.
compatibility_review.required_before_switch: Bounded profile compatibility correction and offline serialized-request review. Further paid measurements would exceed this completed six-request authorization.
